To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
multimeric bivalently glycoconjugates from recombinant carrier proteins and synthetic hexasacchrides can be prepared by a simple, fast, and efficient reaction.

we have developed a method for preparing well-defined multivalent immunogens with predictable glycan:protein ratio, whose molecular weight and the amount of saccharides attached could be independently controlled.

we have developed a method for preparation of multimeric bivalently glycosylated immunogens from recom­binant tetanus toxoid fragment (rTT), synthetic oligosaccharides, synthetic glycopeptide ad­ju­vants and squaric acid as the conjugation agent, and we have demonstrated that the immunogens prepared in this manner induce a protective immune response against Vibrio cholera.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation of well-defined multimeric bivalently glycosylated immunogens, with the aim of developing conjugate vaccines for the prevention of diseases caused by bacterial pathogens.
the design and preparation of novel multivalent immunogens from synthetic carbohydrates and recombinant carrier proteins.
the development of multivalent carbohydrate-based vaccines for bacterial diseases, such as cholera and meningitis, from synthetic carbohydrates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the immunogenicity of the multivalent immunogens prepared in this work is comparable to the best of the existing vaccines against bacterial diseases, such as cholera and tetanus.
the immunogenicity of multimeric bivalently conjugated rTT-HC is superior to that of the monovalent rTT-HC, and that the multivalent rTT-HC conjugates are more potent than the monovalent ones.
multivalent glycoconjugates are a very promising tool for the design of vaccines against bacterial diseases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the synthetic carbohydrates are not only useful as probes to monitor the conjugation reaction, but can also be used as adjuvant in the preparation of multivalent vaccines.
we have developed a new method for preparation of multimeric neoglycoepitopes and demonstrated its applicability for preparation of multivalent conjugate vaccine candidates.
multimeric bivalency, in combination with the use of a synthetic glycopeptide as adjuvant, can be used to prepare immunogens that elicit strong immune response to the carbohydrate antigen.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the synthetic carbohydrate adjuvant is as potent as the natural peptidoglican adjuvant, but the synthetic hexasacharide fragment of O:1 Inaba is a much more potent antigen than the corresponding fragment of the O:1 Ogawa serotype.

the use of synthetic oligosaccharides in combination with rTT-HC and a synthetic adjuvant can lead to the preparation of multimeric bivalently glycosylated immunogens that induce strong and long-lived immune responses.
the synthetic carbohydrates can be used as immunogens and that they can be used as adjuvants.
